question.problem:
Consider the matrix $A$ for which ${\lambda }_{1}=-2$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-1$ are eigenvalues, and

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4\end{aligned}]
$$

are the respective eigenvectors. What are the values of $a,b,c$ given that

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & b \\ c & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}a & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}1 & b \\ c & -4\end{aligned}]}^{-1}?
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14152180/assets/4d74ff9020d9196bcc9e63011652b70c718d150fd69f0bc47d5e31e5f2c73900.svg) ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14152180/assets/5516abd511f6e76c0453294f9822ea87a743df25dcfb9c9078447c80b3ae1aa5.svg) are the respective eigenvectors. Find the matrices $P$ and $D$ such that $PDP^{-1} = A,$ where $D$ is a diagonal matrix.
current_example.worked_solution:
Since the eigenvalues of the matrix are $\lambda_1={\color{blue}4}$ and $\lambda_2={\color{red}3},$ we construct the diagonal matrix $D$ by writing the eigenvalues in the main diagonal:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14152180/assets/9feff06a6d717e5f56fbfedcec44ebb57d4240192202fda3f3537a36d222f5ee.svg)

Now, to construct the matrix $P,$ we simply write the respective eigenvectors as columns: 

- the $1$st column is the eigenvector corresponding to $\lambda_1={\color{blue}4},$ and

- the $2$nd column is the eigenvector corresponding to $\lambda_2={\color{red}3}.$

Therefore, we get
